newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong money rates ease, gov't paper prices up.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong money rates ease, gov't paper prices up.

text.p: Hong Kong interbank rates fell across the board and government paper prices firmed after the U.S. Federal Reserve decided to maintain interest rates unchanged overnight, dealers said on Wednesday.
"But the rate fall was slightly narrower than those in the U.S. markets," a local bank dealer said.
Overnight cash eased to 5-3/16 1/16 percent from 5-5/16 3/16 at midday on Tuesday and three month money fell 1/16 to 5-9/16 7/16 percent.
"Active offering interest is seen in the swap market but the cash market is relatively calm," a Japanese bank dealer said.
The news was not totally unexpected with some dealers still believing the United States would not raise interest rates before the presidential election in November.
"I don't think they will lift rates until the presidential election is over," one said.
But others said the Fed's action lagged behind the market and pushed the yield curve steeper.
Sentiment remained cautious and the market awaited more clues from U.S. economic indicators as dealers differed on the U.S. interest rate trend.
The overnight rate was seen underpinned by month-end demand and should maintain its current level until early October, dealers said.
Trading of government paper was active with early buying interest alternating with profit-taking at highs, dealers said.
The seven-year note yielded 7.60 percent against 7.66, the five-year 7.26 versus 7.33 and the three-year 6.60 vs 6.68.
One-week bill edged one basis point down to 5.07.
